title: SLO observability pipeline design and validation
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines a canonical design and validation workflow for the SLO observability pipeline used by Redwood Inference SRE. It covers metric selection, collection guarantees, aggregation/rollups, validation and backfill procedures, automated error-budget actions, and runbook primitives for SLO burn incidents. The goal is to ensure SLOs are measurable, auditable, and actionable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide an end-to-end pattern for converting raw telemetry into trusted SLO state and automated operational responses.
- Scope: All production services that expose external-facing customer APIs (text generation, embeddings, chat) and internal platform surfaces that carry user-visible traffic (control plane routes). Does not cover purely experimental or internal feature branches.

Key terms:
- SLI: Service Level Indicator, the raw metric (ex: successful_response_ratio).
- SLO: Service Level Objective, target on an SLI (ex: 99.95% availability over 30d).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO.
- Burn: sustained error-budget consumption above policy threshold.
- Rollup window: the aggregation interval used for SLO reporting (default 1m -> 5m rollup).

Design principles (non‑negotiable):
1) Deterministic aggregation: every request must map to at most one SLI event with an immutable timestamp and context tags (service, cluster, region, model_variant, route_id, customer_tier).
2) Single source of truth: SLI ingestion must originate from the service emitter and flow through a validated pipeline into the metrics system (Prometheus/Thanos) and the SLO store (Cortex-backed SLO service).
3) Observability parity: SLO-relevant metrics must be present in both real-time alerting (Prometheus) and long-term retrospective stores (Parquet on object storage).
4) Testability & replayability: all ingested raw events are checkpointed for 72 hours to enable replays for validation/backfill.
5) Ownership & audit trail: each SLO has a single owner team and an audit log of changes (who, when, why).

Required telemetry and labels (table):
- name | type | required labels | retention
- request_count | counter | service, route_id, model_variant, region, outcome, status_code | 13 months
- request_latency_ms | histogram | service, route_id, model_variant, region, quantile_tag | 13 months
- kv_cache_hit | counter | service, model_variant, region | 6 months
- upstream_fallback | counter | service, route_id, fallback_reason | 1 year

SLI definitions (examples with PromQL):
1) Availability SLI (success ratio):
- definition: ratio of successful responses to total requests with customer-visible status codes
- PromQL example:
  sum(rate(request_count{service="api-public", outcome=~"success|partial_success"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_count{service="api-public"}[5m]))
2) Latency SLI (p95 tail):
- definition: fraction of requests with latency <= 500ms on production tier routes
- PromQL (using histogram_quantile):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{service="api-public", route_id=~"/v1/.*"}[5m])) by (le)) <= 500
3) Correctness SLI (rerank/semantic scoring):
- definition: automated evaluation success rate for structured outputs on daily sample sets (see "daily-evals" job)

SLO targets and windows (examples):
- api-public availability: target 99.95% over 30d, 99.9% over 7d (secondary)
- embeddings-latency: 95% of requests <= 200ms over 14d
- control-plane-ops: 99.99% availability over 30d
Note: Each SLO must include a rationale paragraph in the SLO metadata explaining customer impact and cost tradeoffs.

Error budget policy and automated actions:
- Soft thresholds (informational): 10% of monthly error budget consumed -> notify owner via Slack SLO channel, generate weekly burn report.
- Hard thresholds (automated mitigation): 25% of monthly error budget consumed -> reduce non-essential background jobs (auto-pause batch refresh), scale down low-priority replication, and enable degraded-mode routing to warm standby models.
- Emergency threshold: 50% of monthly error budget consumed in 24h -> trigger runbook SRV-BURN-01 and open an incident/P1.
- Reconciliation: all automated mitigations must be logged in the SLO audit trail with an auto-generated runbook decision entry.

Validation & backfill workflow (step-by-step):
1) Pre-deploy checks (CI): unit tests for emitters, schema validation for metric labels, and a synthetic traffic job that asserts metric emission at canary load.
2) Canary validation (first 48h): compare canary and baseline SLI rates (delta < 0.05%). If deviation > 0.2% open a preflight review.
3) Backfill/replay steps when gaps detected:
   a) Identify gap window from checkpointed raw events.
   b) Replay events into a validation namespace and compute SLI.
   c) If replay SLI differs from production SLO by > 0.1% for availability or > 2% for latency quantiles, escalate to SRE and platform-observability.
   d) Once fixed, record a backfill job and annotate the SLO with the correction.
4) Post-deploy audit (30d): scheduled SLO-quality report comparing metric drift, cardinality growth, and rollup accuracy.

Runbook primitives (short snippets):
- SLO-BURN-ALERT (P2)
  1) Pager fires when 25% monthly budget consumed AND 14d budget slope > 0.5%/day.
  2) Triage: confirm signal (run PromQL queries, check for client-side retry storms).
  3) Immediate mitigations: route to lower-cost model_variant, enable prefix KV cache bypass, disable non-critical telemetry.
  4) If mitigations reduce burn rate to <10%/day, move to monitoring state; otherwise escalate to on-call P1.

- SLO-BACKFILL (Runbook)
  1) Owner tags the SLO and requests replay from the checkpoint store.
  2) Validation lead runs replay in staging namespace, generating a JSON report (schema below).
  3) If consistent, merge backfill and update SLO notes.

Alert rule YAML example (PrometheusAlertmanager-style):
- alert: SLO_MonthlyBudgetBurnHigh
  expr: (1 - (sum(rate(request_count{service="api-public", outcome=~"success|partial_success"}[30d])) / sum(rate(request_count{service="api-public"}[30d])))) > 0.0025
  for: 30m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    runbook: SRV-BURN-01
  annotations:
    summary: "SLO monthly burn > 25% for api-public"

Metric quality gates (automated checks executed nightly):
- cardinality growth < 15% week-over-week per service
- required labels present on 99.9% of samples
- histogram bucket completeness (no missing buckets for last 7 days)
- replay parity: replayed SLI within 0.1% of live SLI for availability metrics

Operational tooling integrations (recommended):
- Checkpoint store: S3 bucket with lifecycle 90d for raw events, archived Parquet for 13 months.
- Replay engine: containerized job (replayctl) that accepts window and SLO id and writes to validation Prometheus namespace.
- SLO dashboard: Cortex-based SLO store surfaced in Redwood Console with token-level filters.
- Automation: a lightweight runner (runbook-exec) to apply the automated mitigation actions via infra API.

Ownership, audits and change control:
- Every SLO must live in the SLO registry and include: owner, escalation channel, rationale, and approval history.
- Changes to SLO thresholds require: owner sign-off + SRE peer review + a 72h monitoring window post-change.
- Audit record sample: "2025-01-21 | Maya Patel | raised availability target for api-public from 99.9->99.95 | reason: enterprise SLA increase"

On-call playbook excerpt (when called from PagerDuty):
1) Acknowledge and capture initial facts: affected routes, burn rate, recent deploys, and capacity signals.
2) Run the triage notebook (link in SLO dashboard) that executes canonical PromQL queries and summarizes upstream errors, client retry patterns, and capacity headroom.
3) If evidence points to capacity saturation, coordinate with capacity on-call to run quick scale (see capacity rapid scale checklist).
4) Notify product & customer success if an incident is declared (include estimated customer impact and mitigation timeline).

Rollout checklist for the observability pipeline (preflight):
- emitter library updated and released
- CI metric schema checks pass
- checkpointing to S3 enabled for the service
- canary traffic tests green for 48h
- SLO created in registry with owner and rationale
- automated mitigations reviewed and simulated in staging

Appendix: example JSON report schema for replay validation (single-line fields):
- replay_id, slo_id, start_ts, end_ts, baseline_availability, replay_availability, diff_pct, action_taken

Related references:
- SLO escalation and capacity triggers (internal page)
- Error budget orchestration playbook (internal page)

Document maintenance:
- Owner: engineering (SRE); review cadence: quarterly or after any major SLO incident.
- Last review: 2025-02-03 (Maya Patel).
